reviews.text: It's incredibly expensive, and they'll try to get you to pay you under any pretext. I recommend it to people who have money and those who don't question what their doctors say (people who don't realize they're being exploited).

We have been using your services since the time of our previous dog. Our previous dog, a dachshund (18 years old), passed away at home, and we had a grooming appointment scheduled. When we contacted you, you immediately sent us a bouquet of flowers and a letter, which deeply touched our whole family.

We recently welcomed a new puppy and had her spayed. The pre-operative examinations were thorough, and we felt completely at ease entrusting her to your care. The spaying surgery was successful, and she is doing well. Besides the doctor, all the staff are incredibly kind.

It was quite a while ago, but my regular vet was closed, so I went to another vet in a hurry. A young male vet injected my dog ​​with morphine, which made him lose consciousness, and he died about a week later. I was told that the morphine was shock therapy because my dog ​​had lost sensation in his lower back, so I agreed, but now I can't help but wonder if I was being experimented on. I will never go there again.
Thank you for using our services. We are very pleased with your high rating. Please feel free to visit us again if you have any health concerns in the future.
Thank you for your continued support. I appreciate how you always explain things so carefully, and I'm grateful that there are so many teachers to offer different opinions.

I was worried my cat might be sick and I came here for the first time. Sensei was very nice and she made sure to do all the necessary tests, even though my cat was scared and attacked everyone. She also translated everything to English as my Japanese is very bad. She also even thought of giving me a sedative medication for the next time, as it was difficult to bring my cat to the vet. This was overall a better experience than most small neighborhood clinics I have been to before.

Ultimately, my pet died because of this hospital. I absolutely would not recommend it to anyone who owns small animals.

When I sought a second opinion, it turned out that the uterus hadn't been completely removed, which caused cancer. Furthermore, there was a veterinarian who insisted on being able to treat animals perfectly, even though they couldn't, and made two misdiagnoses. When I mentioned the symptoms I suspected, they denied it, and the medication they prescribed was, of course, ineffective, leaving my pet in a life-or-death situation. (Later, it turned out my suspicions were correct.) When I told the branch manager about it, there was no apology. Looking back and comparing it to the second opinion, I realize how terrible what happened was. I feel so sorry for my pet, and every time I remember, I'm filled with regret and can't stop crying.

Also, initially, they performed procedures in front of us, but after a few years, they kept my pet in their care and performed procedures out of our sight. Apparently, this is unheard of at other hospitals. Were they using my pet as a practice dummy? Do they become careless after seeing animals for so many years? I wish they would treat each pet with a little more care. I don't even want to give them one star.

Thank you for your continued support. The doctors and nurses are very caring, and it's a great hospital. Waiting times may vary depending on the day, but generally, you won't have to wait too long on weekdays. It's close to my house, so I always go on foot or by bicycle, and I haven't had any trouble finding parking so far. I think it's a trustworthy hospital.
The teacher takes good care of them.

I used to take my dog ​​to the vet once a month to have its anal glands expressed. I had the same vet express the glands twice in a row, and both times they squeezed until there was a lot of blood. Even though the anal sacs were slightly hard and there was a possibility of inflammation, was it really necessary to express them so thoroughly? The vet dismissed the amount of bleeding as nothing to worry about and didn't even check the dog's history of anal sac inflammation. If the owner hadn't requested it, the vet wouldn't have prescribed anything. I'm not an expert in veterinary medicine, so my point of view may not necessarily be correct, but I don't think the owner will be satisfied with this. Incidentally, the vet doesn't have a very good reputation among my dog-walking friends either.
